[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant recommended the following language learning apps:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Duolingo: A gamified app for interactive lessons, quizzes, and exercises (Free, iOS and Android).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Babbel: A comprehensive app focusing on conversational skills (Subscription-based, iOS and Android).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Quizlet: A study app with flashcards, tests, and study games (Free, iOS and Android).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. HelloTalk: A language exchange app connecting users with native speakers (Free, iOS and Android).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Memrise: A spaced repetition app using memes and gamification (Free, iOS and Android).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant recommended the following online resources:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. BBC Learning English: A comprehensive website with audio and video lessons, quizzes, and games (Free).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. English Central: A video-based platform for practicing speaking and listening (Free, with premium features).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Grammarly Handbook: A free online guide to English grammar, punctuation, and writing style (Free).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. TED Talks with subtitles: For improving listening and reading comprehension (Free).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. English language YouTube channels: Channels like EnglishClass101, LearnEnglish with Emma, and Rachel's English (Free).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided additional tips for practice:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Set aside time each day to practice, even if it's just for 10-15 minutes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Focus on one or two resources at a time to avoid feeling overwhelmed.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Practice active listening and speaking by repeating what you hear or speaking with native speakers.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Use flashcards or vocabulary apps to learn new words and phrases.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Read English texts
